fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Checking retained CD weave length against design-year weaving volume is a core preliminary-design safety check for cloverleaf conversions; concentrated lane-change conflicts are a genuine, well-recognised hazard.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-001 is cited as defining the requirement and the volume assumption references a traffic data input, but the quote is null and the 80 m extension figure carries no derivational support.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern under the explicitly qualified international baseline; no normative basis claimed and no conflation of compliance checks with the safety issue.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Dual option of an 80 m lengthening or ramp metering is specific, actionable and viable, though the 80 m is unexplained and diverges from the statement's 'signalise the CD exit' alternative.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on a grade-separated CD weaving section; scoping road_users to vehicle occupants acknowledges the restricted user population, though no explicit VRU-exclusion note is given.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled path-user crossings at free-flow ramp terminals are a genuine, well-recognised interchange safety hazard, correctly flagged at preliminary design when crossing strategy can still be shaped.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-001 is cited but with no quote and context-only use, so the specific claims (retained loops, shared-use path, 'northern loop-ramp') rest on an unverifiable contextual anchor rather than quoted recorded facts.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly held as a categorical safety_concern under the qualified PIARC-derived international baseline, with no spurious normative citation (normative_basis_note appropriately null) and no compliance conflation.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Signalising the northern loop-ramp crossing is specific and viable, but 'raised tables elsewhere' is vague in count/location and questionable on free-flow ramp geometry, while the grade-separated option named in the statement is dropped.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are both explicitly identified as affected road users and the entire finding is structured around their crossing continuity and exposure, so VRU impacts are fully considered.
